title: Baba Bakala
hookLine: where Makhan Shah found the ninth Guru

lines: NOT THE LOUDEST. THE QUIET ONE.
cards: A man stands on a rooftop in a village, shouting to everyone below: the Guru is found! The Guru is found! Down in the lanes, people stop and look up, and a few of them are not happy to hear it.
The village is Bakala, near the Beas. The man on the roof is a trader named Makhan Shah. And the one he found was not the loudest man in the village.
He was the one sitting quietly.

teach.b: First, a riddle of two words. Tradition says the child Guru, Guru Har Krishan, as he was dying in Delhi, was asked who would come after him. He answered only: Baba Bakale.
The Baba is in Bakala. Second, the crowd.
When word spread, tradition says, many men in Bakala set up seats and called themselves the Guru, each with his own followers and his own claims. It was noisy, and it was confusing. Third, the test.
This path has met Makhan Shah before, as a trader. Tradition says that in a storm at sea he had promised an offering to the Guru if his ship came through.
In Bakala he didn't know whom to give it to, so he went from seat to seat, leaving each claimant a small gift and saying nothing of his promise. They took it, and thanked him.
Then he came to Tegh Bahadur, a man who, tradition says, spent long hours in quiet meditation in a small room below ground. And Tegh Bahadur reminded him of the full promise he had made.
That's when Makhan Shah ran up to the roof. Fourth, the teaching underneath. Guru Tegh Bahadur, the ninth Guru, later wrote hymns that are in the Guru Granth Sahib.

teach.h: GIVE UP THE PRIDE OF THE MIND.
teach.b: In one, he says, in paraphrase: holy people, give up the pride of the mind.
The one who was found had not been looking to be found. Today a gurdwara stands at Baba Bakala, and Sikhs visit the place tradition remembers as that underground room.

how: Sikhs visit Gurdwara Baba Bakala Sahib and the place tradition remembers as Guru Tegh Bahadur's room of meditation, and they tell the story of Makhan Shah, especially around the ninth Guru's gurpurab.

s: the ninth Guru announced himself loudly in Bakala
tradition says he was the quiet one, meditating, while many others set up seats.
Makhan Shah's test came from a promise he'd made in a storm
only the true Guru, tradition says, would know the full promise.
Baba Bakale was the name of a man
it was the child Guru's two-word answer: the Baba is in Bakala.

games.q: you're Makhan Shah in Bakala, with many men each saying he is the Guru. how do you find the right one?
o: follow the one with the biggest crowd.
give each a small gift and wait for one to name your promise.
games.why: tradition says he left a small gift at each seat, and only Tegh Bahadur reminded him of the full promise.

practice: Bring to mind a room you were in recently, a meeting, a family dinner, a group chat, and notice who took up the most space. Then let that voice fade a little and look for the quiet one, the person who said one thing or nothing.
Stay with them for a few breaths, and wonder what they were noticing that nobody asked about.

wordCard.voice: Baba Bakala. The village near the Beas where, tradition says, Makhan Shah found Guru Tegh Bahadur among many claimants, and shouted it from the roof. Today's word.

orig.note: Punjabi: the Baba is in Bakala. the child Guru's answer, tradition says.

carryVoice: Your line: the guru found. The quietest seat in the village held the answer. See you tomorrow.
